point_a: A parent of an 11th grader who has seen '+200 points guaranteed' ads, suspects the rules are buried on a terms page, has maybe paid for prep before and watched the homework stop after week two, and has no way to tell what is happening until the score arrives.
point_b: Karman shows the whole deal before I talk to anyone (price, dates, every rule of the guarantee as a number), it ends on my kid's test date, and I will see every week whether the work got done. Next step: book the free practice test on December 12.

enemy.statement: The usual SAT prep sells open-ended hours or subscriptions, prints a big guarantee and hides its rules on a separate page, then stops watching once you have paid. Karman sells a program that ends on one SAT date, prints every rule as a number, and reports the work to the parent every week.

facts.fact: Every cohort ends on one official SAT date: March 6, 2027, then May 1 and June 5.
Classes are capped at six students: five paid seats and one scholarship seat.
18 live classes of 90 minutes, two a week (Tuesday and Thursday 7:00 to 8:30 p.m. ET, still marked CONFIRM).
Five full-length practice tests, each followed by a 60-minute one-on-one review of every missed question.
Daily 10: every missed question returns after 2, 7 and 21 days.
Parents get a weekly update: practice time, attendance, test scores and next steps.
The guarantee: +100 points or a 1450. Half or all of the price back, or the next cohort free; the family chooses.
The guarantee has five student rules, each a number tracked on the dashboard: 15 of 18 classes, all 5 reviews, all 5 tests, 90% of practice, sit the SAT.

Competitor guarantees (read from their own terms pages, 2026-10 research) include 100% homework rules, poll quotas, same-device rules, 'good faith' clauses and 'submitting a claim doesn't guarantee approval'. Karman's guarantee has none of these.
A claim is one email with the official College Board report within 30 days; nothing is taken out of a refund.
March cohort: $995 founding price, or 3 payments of $345; $1,295 for later cohorts; a $100 refundable deposit holds a seat.
Private 10 is $1,450 and Private 20 is $2,900 ($145 an hour).
Free practice test: Saturday, December 12, 10:00 a.m. ET, about 75 minutes, 49 Karman questions, live proctor on Zoom, estimated score range, domain breakdown, 20-minute results call.
Karman 1:1 tutoring: +285 points on average (1235 to 1520), 94% reached their target, median 16 weeks, 1,200+ students tutored.
Students at 1500+ or under four weeks from the test are told a program probably isn't worth their money.
Karman is named for the Karman line, 100 km up, where the atmosphere ends and space begins.

cut: 'The climb starts before sunrise.' Beautiful film line, but a parent can't falsify it and any brand could sign it.
'10,000+ original practice questions.' Live count was 2,588 on 2026-10-19; the release check blocks the claim. Written around until the bank reaches it.
'We don't sell hours. We sell March 6.' Two-beat antithesis, banned by copy rule 16.
'Cameras on, questions answered live.' No fact says cameras are required.
'Our tutors know every name.' Talk, not a fact.
caveats: Every specific in this copy traces to a fact you provided or a review you supplied — check them before you spend money behind them. This writes the copy; it doesn't verify your claims or clear them for compliance.
